summary: A0010 applied at the SPEC layer to exactly the four named PLANNED tasks and nothing else. In the planning worktree /home/lpdev/lp-worktrees/amendment-a0010-attempt-001, git status --porcelain shows exactly four modified tracked paths - docs/spec/strategy/STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md, docs/spec/research/DATASET_AND_EVALUATION.md, todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T064.md and todo/phases/P06-backtesting-and-strategy/T065.md - plus the controller's own untracked .workflow/amendment-request.json; todo/config.yaml, every other contract, docs/intent/, docs/implement/, tools/, tests/, .claude/ and todo/schemas/ are byte-identical to base, so no status, attempt, commit SHA, evidence pointer, review record, approval datum or dependency field moved and no task was activated or consumed an attempt. T101 and T102 were deliberately left byte-identical to base; the basis for each is stated in the rationale. (1) STRATEGY_ECONOMICS.md section 7 now names only names that exist or are assigned to a task and states the boundary and its owner. The list is now AdmissionSnapshot, MarketSnapshot, PortfolioSnapshot (inputs; src/robinhood_lp/strategy/base.py:557, 636, 727, and T060's unchanged deliverable 'immutable, versioned admission/market/portfolio snapshots'), RegimeModel and FeeOpportunityModel (components; base.py:831, 862), and RegimeAssessment, FeeOpportunityAssessment, CandidateAction (outputs; base.py:894, 1017, 1152). StrategyDecision is no longer listed among the components: it is the backtest engine's callback return type (src/robinhood_lp/backtest/engine.py:198) and now appears only in the paragraph that describes the engine boundary. AdmissionEligibilitySnapshot, MarketFeatureSnapshot, CandidatePolicy and EconomicEvaluator had no occurrence anywhere in the repository outside that one list (repository-wide grep, including yaml/json and the whole todo tree) and are gone; PortfolioSnapshot, previously omitted, is named. The rule that a component name never denotes an output and vice versa is kept and attributed to T060. The new paragraph states which of the two boundaries a backtest actually crosses today - the event-driven engine's strategy callback, which is handed a StrategyDecisionRequest (visible events plus ledger; engine.py:175) and must return a StrategyDecision (injected as strategy_callback, engine.py:436) - and that the engine never calls the snapshot/component boundary directly. It assigns the adapter between the two boundaries to T065, whose contract now carries the matching deliverable sentence and a section-7 pointer in its References. (2) DS-030 no longer cites the retired ten-million-block window: the small model families are justified by the per-pool extended-history window ADR-015 establishes (each member pool's own Initialize block to the run's agreed finalized block, width set by that pool's history rather than a fixed width), with only numbers that follow from that window - the measured 0.1008-second block interval, the pinned reference pool's roughly 12 days or about 3.4 thousand five-minute bars and 288 hourly bars, and the roughly 76 days of total mainnet history which caps any single-pool window at about 22 thousand five-minute bars. The substance is kept: the measured sample size is the binding constraint and a multi-pool panel is dominated by a small number of shared market regimes. (3) ECO-REGIME-001 now gives the already-confirmed above-100-percent rule the same treatment OPERATOR_CONTROL.md gives the minus-80-percent rule: the same formula computed at the end of the period (return_5m = close_usdg / open_usdg - 1), completeness required so that an incomplete period cannot trigger it, and a strictly greater than 100% trigger. It states that both confirmed five-minute rules share one formula, one bar convention, the same T053-qualified point-in-time USDG five-minute K-line series and its 300-second window, and the same boundary-alignment and clock convention the T050 bar layer already requires (window boundary aligned to an integer multiple of the window length in the bar's own clock, bars carrying data time and availability time, no wall-clock read in the rule judgement), differing only in threshold direction and in response ownership. (4) The halt-or-degrade obligation now has exactly one home: it is defined in docs/spec/research/DATASET_AND_EVALUATION.md as the new clause DS-035 (section 5), and T064's contract was reduced to a reference to it in Deliverables, Acceptance and References, so the two documents no longer both define it. T064 keeps the scenario catalogue itself as its deliverable and keeps its acceptance criterion that each failure scenario halts or degrades exactly as its declaration says, with DS-041's floor against undefined behaviour and forced trades intact. No Must not clause, acceptance criterion, or safety, risk, promotion or precision rule was removed or relaxed anywhere; every edit adds coverage, replaces a retired basis with the current one, or makes an existing requirement explicit.
rationale: Owner-direction mapping, item by item, with the repository fact each change rests on. (1) Section 7 named seven entries as 'substitutable components'. Three of those statements were false against the repository: StrategyDecision is not a component but the engine's callback return type (engine.py:198, and T060's unchanged section states that a component name never denotes an output and an output name never denotes a component); AdmissionEligibilitySnapshot and MarketFeatureSnapshot exist nowhere else, while the implemented and contract-specified inputs are AdmissionSnapshot, MarketSnapshot and PortfolioSnapshot (base.py:557, 636, 727; T060 Deliverables), so section 7 both used two names nothing else uses and omitted PortfolioSnapshot; CandidatePolicy and EconomicEvaluator had no task, acceptance, code or reference anywhere (verified by grep with and without file filters). The corrected list therefore names exactly the three versioned inputs, the two substitute components and the three outputs that exist and are contract-specified, drops the two unassigned names rather than inventing a task for them, keeps the component/output naming rule (attributed to T060, which attributes its own vocabulary to this section), and moves StrategyDecision to the boundary paragraph where it is the engine's return type. Adapter ownership was decided from recorded repository evidence, not preference: T061's developer evidence (an APPROVED task's record) says 'The strategy layer's T060 CandidateAction contract is not yet consumed by the engine; T062 / T065 will wire the concrete strategy components into the same callback shape' (todo/evidence/P06/T061/attempt-001-developer.json:32); T062's developer evidence records that the baselines consume StrategyDecisionRequest rather than the T060 snapshots and that 'none such adapter exists today, and the T060 contracts do not provide a StrategyCallback-shaped entry point' (todo/evidence/P06/T062/attempt-001-developer.json:36) - that is exactly the gap, since T062 is APPROVED and uneditable and already delivered its callback-shaped baselines; and the sequencing forces the crossing into Phase 6, because T066 (dependencies T064 and T065) produces PnL, profit-probability, Expected-Shortfall, boundary and time-in-Range distributions, which are engine-run artifacts of the T065 strategy, and T065's own acceptance requires every decision to replay from its manifest, a T063 run artifact. T065 is therefore named as the adapter owner, and for the same reason one sentence was added to T065's Deliverables and a section-7 pointer to its References: the correction makes T065's text wrong by omission, because its contract never said how the rule strategy reaches the engine even though it must be engine-evaluated before T102 exists; this is the clause the direction allows and the basis is stated here. T102's text was not adjusted and is not made wrong: it says the model occupies the replaceable regime and fee-opportunity interfaces the strategy contract already defines and changes nothing else, and its walk-forward evaluation is driven through the engine behind the same adapter, which the specification it already references now names. T101's text was not adjusted either: A0009 already re-based its sample-size disclosure on ADR-015 ('per pool, from that pool's own Initialize block to the run's agreed finalized block', roughly 3.4 thousand five-minute bars or 288 hourly bars at the measured 0.1008-second interval), which is the same window and the same numbers the corrected DS-030 now states, so no contract text contradicts the specification. No dependency edge was added or removed anywhere, and none is required by these edits: the corrected text asserts no consumption relationship that the existing Dependencies blocks and config.yaml depends_on sets do not already express. (2) ADR-015 clause 5 retires the min(end - 10_000_000, Initialize) start and states that no later clause may cite the ten-million-block window as the research range; DS-030's justification was the last surviving citation of it as a research range, and it also carried a derived figure (11.7 days) that belonged to the retired rule. The replacement uses only ADR-015's own measurements and the arithmetic that follows from the window it establishes: each pool's window runs from its Initialize block to the run's agreed finalized block, the measured interval is 0.1008 seconds, the pinned reference pool gives about 12 days or about 3.4 thousand five-minute bars (288 hourly), and the chain's total history of about 76 days caps any single-pool window at about 22 thousand five-minute bars. The justification's substance is unchanged: the model families stay deliberately small because the measured sample size is the binding constraint and a multi-pool panel is dominated by a few shared market states. No threshold, model-scope or deep-learning-exclusion statement was touched. (3) OPERATOR_CONTROL.md CTRL-MARKET-001 defines its minus-80-percent condition as a complete bar's close over open minus one, computed at the end of the period, with an unfinished period forbidden to trigger it (docs/spec/operations/OPERATOR_CONTROL.md:101-103), while the strategy specification's above-100-percent rule had no formula and no bar convention. The strategy clause now states the identical formula and completeness rule and fixes the trigger as strictly greater than 100 percent, which is what PROJECT_GOALS.md G-STRATEGY-SPIKE-01 says ('涨幅超过 100%') and what the implemented rule does: FIVE_MINUTE_UP_SPIKE_FRACTION is 100 percent in Q64.64 and the verdict is raised only when the post price exceeds the pre price and the move is strictly greater than the threshold (src/robinhood_lp/features/quote.py:104, 1548), with FIVE_MINUTE_RULE_WINDOW_SECONDS = 300 (quote.py:97) for both rules. The added sentence answers the alignment-and-clock question with the repository's own convention instead of inventing one: the bar layer requires a window boundary aligned to an integer multiple of the window length in the bar's own clock and refuses non-aligned ends (src/robinhood_lp/features/bars.py:1617, 1643), bars carry data time and availability time, and ADR-006 plus ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 keep wall-clock reads out of deterministic paths, so both rules read the same series and no second bar definition is created. Nothing was widened: the rule stays strictly-in-strategy, non-global, and the minus-80-percent breaker stays the only AUTO_EXIT condition of the pair. (4) The halt-or-degrade obligation was placed in the specification rather than left in T064's contract because it is evaluation-run discipline that is not specific to one task: it binds any robustness, stress or anti-overfitting run, it is the same class of rule as DS-031 (declare before you look) and DS-041 (degradation must be deterministic and never undefined behaviour or a forced trade), and both of those already live in DS sections rather than in contracts - DS-041 is in fact the clause T064's acceptance already cites as its floor. Keeping it in the contract would have left the T101 harness and T102 walk-forward runs, which inject failure and boundary cases of their own, with no shared obligation. The new clause DS-035 says each declared scenario must have exactly one declared outcome before the run - a halt with a named reason code, or a deterministic fallback named by that entry - recorded in one place and never inferred or improvised afterwards, and repeats DS-041's prohibition on undefined behaviour and forced trades. T064 keeps the scenario catalogue itself (which cases, which named fallback per entry) as its deliverable and keeps its acceptance criterion, now citing DS-035 for the obligation and DS-041 for the floor, so the two documents reference one definition instead of carrying two. Every edit was checked to add or tighten: no Must not clause, acceptance criterion, or safety, risk, promotion or precision rule was deleted or weakened, the retired ten-million-block window is removed rather than restated, and no retired task, no credential, key material, environment value or URL was written. Investigation performed in the planning worktree, reported as investigation only and never as acceptance evidence: python -m tools.workflow validate returns status OK; git diff --check is clean; tests/test_documentation_links.py and tests/test_workflow_contracts.py pass 6/6, which includes the checks that every contract keeps exactly one of each required section and that its Dependencies section still matches todo/config.yaml. One non-blocking observation, outside this amendment's layer and not a required change: T102's Dependencies block lists T061 and T101 only, while its References and acceptance compare the model against T065's rule implementation through the adapter T065 now owns; that is a pre-existing plan-structure question (a dependency field and a config.yaml depends_on entry, neither of which this SPEC-layer direction permits touching), and it does not block or weaken anything written here.
